question.problem: A certain disease is present in $500$ out of $100\,000$ people in city $A,$ $800$ out of $200\,000$ people in city $B,$ and $1\,100$ out of $500\,000$ people in city $C.$ What is the probability that a randomly selected person from any city has the disease?
question.worked_solution:
Let $D$ be the event that a person has the disease, and

- let $A$ be the event that the person is from city $A,$

- let $B$ be the event that the person is from city $B,$

- let $C$ be the event that the person is from city $C.$

Then the disjoint union $A⊔B⊔C$ covers the entire sample space.

To calculate the probability that a randomly selected person has the disease, we use the law of total probability:

$$
P(D)=P(D\cap A)+P(D\cap B)+P(D\cap C)
$$

First, notice that there are a total of 

$$
100\,000+200\,000+500\,000=800\,000
$$

people in all three cities.

- To calculate $P(D\cap A),$ we take the number of people in city $A$ who have the disease $(500)$ and divide by the total number of people in the three cities $(800\,000).$ So, we have

$$
P(D\cap A)=\frac{500}{800\,000}.
$$

- To calculate $P(D\cap B),$ we take the number of people in city $B$ who have the disease $(800)$ and divide by the total number of people in the three cities $(800\,000).$ So, we have

$$
P(D\cap B)=\frac{800}{800\,000}.
$$

- To calculate $P(D\cap C),$ we take the number of people in city $C$ who have the disease $(1\,100)$ and divide by the total number of people in the three cities $(800\,000).$ So, we have

$$
P(D\cap C)=\frac{1\,100}{800\,000}.
$$

Finally, substituting the above information into the law of total probability, the probability that a randomly selected person from any city has the disease is

$$
\begin{aligned}P(D) & =P(D\cap A)+P(D\cap B)+P(D\cap C) \\  & =\frac{500}{800\,000}+\frac{800}{800\,000}+\frac{1\,100}{800\,000} \\  & =\frac{2\,400}{800\,000} \\  & =\frac{24}{8\,000} \\  & =\frac{3}{1\,000}.\end{aligned}
$$
